title: Quadratic-Time Diagonal Simulator
statement: There exists a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet that simulates every language in $mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ on inputs of length $n$ within a constant multiple of $(T(n)+n+1)^2$ steps for all sufficiently large $n$: for every time bound $T$ and every such language $L$, if $L\in\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$, then there are natural numbers $A$ and $N_0$ such that for every $n\ge N_0$ some binary string $x$ of length $n$ is decided by the machine in $A(T(n)+n+1)^2$ steps.
